# Main Page {.unnumbered}

This is a living map of the tools, models, harnesses, and practices that matter for building reliable agentic systems. It favors things you can run yourself, keep under your control, and host on your own hardware or a cheap [{{< glossary "(VPS) Virtual Private Server" display="VPS" popup="hover" >}}](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#vps-virtual-private-server).

## What this book is for

Most writing about AI agents still treats the model as the system. In practice the model is only one layer. What determines whether an agent is useful or fragile is the surrounding stack: the harness that drives the loop, the tools and sandboxes it can reach, the memory it retains, and the governance that keeps it from doing damage.

This book is for people who want to **assemble and control** that stack rather than just call an API.

- Solo developers and indie builders who want a personal agent they can actually trust
- Teams introducing agentic workflows with clear boundaries and observability
- Practitioners who prefer local-first and self-hosted options when they are viable
